detailZh: 哈贾尔：红牛车手的伤病恢复正按计划进行，车队在阿塞拜疆大奖赛决定前提供下一步更新
红牛车队的哈贾尔因手腕受伤，自夏休期以来已缺席三场比赛；车队将在巴库站前评估Hadjar是否准备好回归；9月24日至26日，通过天空体育 F1直播观看阿塞拜疆大奖赛的每一节练习赛，正赛在周六举行
红牛车队领队Laurent Mekies表示，他们将继续优先考虑哈贾尔的康复，而不是急于让他从伤病中复出，并计划在下周阿塞拜疆大奖赛前进行评估，然后再决定他是否参赛。
Hadjar在夏休期后赛事恢复前的常规训练中手腕受伤，因此缺席了最近三场比赛。小红牛车队的劳森代替他出战。
在上周日的西班牙大奖赛后，梅基斯表示哈贾尔的康复正按计划进行，并计划安排一次模拟器训练，以帮助评估他是否准备好重返巴库的比赛。

"Isack的恢复没有任何问题。我认为我们已经了解到，对于他所受的这种伤，这基本上是一个正常的恢复时间，"Mekies说道。
"所以，我们将继续采用同样的方法和我们现有的方案。
"我们将在下周评估情况。
天空体育的克雷格·斯莱特在荷兰大奖赛前解释了伊萨克·哈贾尔的手腕伤势，这是这位法国人首次缺席的比赛。
“我们有一整周，比一整周还多一点的时间，来评估情况，看看他的感觉，然后让他上模拟器，让他接触现实中的限制条件。
“如果他感觉接近百分之百，我们就上。如果他觉得恢复还没完成，我们会坚持把恢复放在首位的做法。
“我们不想做的是，因为过早复出，而损害他长期恢复到百分之百的能力。”
阿塞拜疆大奖赛在巴库的街道赛道上举行，比通常提前一天开始，练习赛将在本周三进行，正赛则在周六。这是三连赛的第一站，随后两个周末将分别在马来西亚和新加坡举行比赛。
红牛对劳森“非常出色”的替补表现感到满意
劳森从姊妹车队小红牛晋升，顶替哈贾尔，这位新西兰人重新回到了他在上赛季初短暂效力两场比赛、但命运不佳的席位。角田裕毅一直为小红牛效力。
劳森两次获得第八名排位，并在赞德福特和马德里都拿到了积分，在马德里他获得第六名。
“我认为他做得非常出色，”Mekies说道。
“我想我们都知道，跳槽到一支不同的车队、驾驶一辆不同的赛车有多么困难，而我认为他已经做到了我们所能期望的最好程度。
“他在马德里]凭借P6拿到了非常重要的积分。他在赞德沃特也做到了同样的事情，而在蒙扎，如果没有与Nico [Hulkenberg]的接触和造成的损伤，他本也能取得类似的成绩。
2026年西班牙大奖赛的亮点
“所以，我认为他做得非常出色。再次强调，与2025年他刚加入车队时的前几场比赛相比，情况已经截然不同，因此我们对此心怀感激，并且感到满意。”
过去一年里，Lawson 在 小红牛 重建了自己的状态和信心，在意外临时重返 红牛 一队之前，他已经享受着一个稳定得分的赛季。
“我认为他作为一名车手持续在成长，”Mekies 补充道，他曾在两支 红牛 车队与 Lawson 共事。“他在车里非常冷静；他非常专注。”
"他当然正在……我不知道他是否为此付出了努力，但他确实在跟随车队的方式以及处理自己表现和赛车表现的方式上，设法让事情保持简单。
"所以，他专注于最核心的事情；他努力把基础做好，而这对他奏效。当然，随着在赛车里的时间增多，你或许可以达到另一个精细度。
"但我认为，那当然是非常、非常强大的。"

detailEn: Isack Hadjar: Red Bull driver's injury recovery going to plan as team provide update on next steps ahead of Azerbaijan GP decision

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar has missed three races since the summer break with an injured wrist; team to assess whether Hadjar is ready to return ahead of Baku; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies says they will continue to prioritise Isack Hadjar's recovery over rushing his return from injury, with evaluations planned before a call on whether he races at next week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Hadjar has missed the last three races after sustaining a wrist injury during routine training ahead of the sport's return to action from its summer break. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson has stood in for him.
Speaking after last Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix, Mekies said Hadjar's recovery was going to plan, with a simulator session planned to help assess his readiness for any return to action in Baku.

"There is nothing wrong with Isack's recovery. I think we have learned that it's fundamentally a normal time for the sort of injuries he has," said Mekies
"So, we will continue with the same approach and what we have.
"We will evaluate the situation in a week's time.
Sky Sports' Craig Slater explained Isack Hadjar's wrist injury ahead of the Dutch GP, the first race the Frenchman missed
"We have a full week, a bit more than a full week, to evaluate situations, to see how he feels and then to put him on the simulator, to expose him to real-life constraints.
"And if he feels close to 100 per cent, we go for it. If he feels the recovery is not completed, we will stick to our approach to put his recovery first.
"What we don't want to do is, by having an early return, compromise his long-term capacity to come back to 100 per cent."

The Azerbaijan GP, held on a street circuit in Baku, starts a day earlier than normal with practice taking place this coming Wednesday ahead of a Saturday race. It is the first round of a triple header with races in Malaysia and Singapore following on the subsequent two weekends.
Red Bull pleased with Lawson's 'very good' stand-in performances

Lawson has stepped up from sister Racing Bulls to cover for Hadjar, with the New Zealander returning to a seat he briefly held in an ill-fated two-race stint at the start of last season. Yuki Tsunoda has been driving for Racing Bulls.
Lawson has twice qualified eighth and scored points at both Zandvoort and Madrid, where he was sixth.
"I think he's done a very good job," said Mekies.
"I think we all know how difficult it is to jump to a different team, to a different car, and I think he has done that to the best of what could have been our expectations.

"He has taken some very important points [in Madrid] with the P6. He did the same in Zandvoort, and in Monza he would have done something similar without the contact with Nico [Hulkenberg] and the damage.
Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix
"So, I think he did a very good job. Again, very different pictures compared to the first races of 2025 when he was in the team, so we are thankful and happy with that."
Lawson has rebuilt his form and confidence at Racing Bulls over the past year and was already enjoying a consistent points-scoring season before his unexpected temporary senior Red Bull return.
"I think he has continued to grow as a driver," added Mekies, who has worked with Lawson at both Red Bull teams. "He's very calm in the car; he's very focused.

"He's certainly making... I don't know if he makes an effort or not [to do it], but he's certainly managed to keep things simple in the way he tracks with the team and in the way he tackles his own performance and the car performance.
"So, he's focused on the essentials; he tries to get the basics right, and it's working for him. Of course, with more time in the car, you can then get to another degree of finesse, maybe.
"But I think that, of course, is very, very strong."

detailEn: United States GP: Lewis Hamilton fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice ahead of Qualifying in Austin

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton outpaced Red Bull's Max Verstappen in final practice in Austin with Friday's pace-setter Charles Leclerc in third; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday
Lewis Hamilton claims the fastest lap from Max Verstappen in final practice at the United States Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton topped final practice from Max Verstappen at the United States Grand Prix to set up a tantalising qualifying in Austin.
Hamilton was 0.168s quicker than Verstappen as Ferrari and Red Bull look set to fight for pole position and victory for a second consecutive weekend.
Charles Leclerc topped both of Friday's sessions and had set the quickest time in final practice by one tenth from Hamilton, only for it to be deleted due to track limits.

Track limits is set to be a major issue for the drivers in qualifying, which takes place at 10pm UK time later on Saturday (build-up from 8.30pm live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event) due to the tarmac run-off areas and the drivers keen to use every bit of track to gain lap time.

Leclerc still finished the session in third, ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli whose chances of becoming the youngest world champion look extremely difficult, given he must first win the Grand Prix to give himself an opportunity, and Mercedes are a tad off the pace.
Antonelli was three tenths behind Hamilton's pace-setting time with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in fifth at nearly half a second down.

McLaren's Lando Norris was eighth but would have been in the top five had his best lap not been deleted for track limit, while Oscar Piastri was sixth and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg impressing in seventh.
